Experimental forecast

Rain outlook for IIT Tirupati campus

Nested WRF model run (9 km, 3 km and 1 km grids) by the HYDROS Lab, started from GFS data of 10 Nov 2026 06:00 UTC (11:30 IST). Shown as the chance of rain in 3-hour blocks, in Indian Standard Time. This run covers 10 Nov 11:30 to 12 Nov 11:30 IST.

Please read: this is a research product, not an official forecast. The model is more useful for saying when rain may come than how much, so no rainfall amounts are shown. The chances below are model-based, not calibrated probabilities. For warnings use IMD (mausam.imd.gov.in).

Next 24 hours (campus area)

…

This run is dry for the campus area. The model gives 0 % chance of rain in every 3-hour block for the 48 hours, on all three grids (9, 3 and 1 km). The rain in this run stays to the south and south-east of the campus, over the Bay of Bengal off the Tamil Nadu coast and near Sri Lanka. A chance of rain is shown only when the model gives at least 1 mm in a 3-hour block, so a short light shower can still be missed, as happened on 10 Nov (see the checks below). This page is not a cyclone forecast; for cyclone and rain warnings follow IMD.

Campus timeline

Chance that rain falls within about 25 km of the campus in each 3-hour block (dashed circle on the map). Taller bar = higher chance. Tap a bar.

rain reported on campusfaded = still to come

Campus reports (field notes): light rain at about 20:30–20:50 IST on 24 Oct, and rain from about 14:30 to 16:00 IST on 25 Oct with some drizzle. IMD gridded rainfall for the campus cell (IMD days run from 08:30 IST to 08:30 IST) was 0.0 mm for each day from 27 Oct to 1 Nov, 4.8 mm for 2 Nov and 21.8 mm for 3 Nov. The 3 Nov value covers the afternoon and night of 2 Nov. Campus reports: only very light drizzle on the night of 29–30 Oct, light rain in the afternoon of 2 Nov, and no rain on 3 Nov until midday. On 4 Nov moderate to heavy rain fell at about 18:00–18:30 IST, followed by drizzle, and moderate rain again from about 21:30 IST. On the night of 5–6 Nov rain fell at some time after midnight (exact time not noted), and light rain fell after about 09:30 IST on 6 Nov, with drizzle at about 13:00 IST. (On the timeline of that earlier run the dots showed this period, not exact times.) For the 11:30–14:30 IST block the model gave about 70 % with a heavier amount possible, but only drizzle was seen; a rain gauge (bucket with a 30 cm opening) put out at about 09:30 IST held about 1.7 mm when read at about 21:20 IST on 6 Nov. Small amounts can partly evaporate, so this is a minimum, but it shows light rain only, not the heavier amount that was possible. No rain was reported after the drizzle at about 13:00 IST up to about 22:00 IST, so the roughly 50 % chance given for 14:30–17:30 IST did not come true.

How to read this · limits
  • What the chance means. Each of the three model grids (9, 3 and 1 km) is checked for the share of its cells within 25 km of the campus that show rain (1 mm or more in the 3 hours; heavier rain means 7.5 mm or more). The three shares are averaged and rounded to the nearest 10 %. Levels: low under 25 %, medium 25–50 %, high 50–75 %, very high above 75 %.
  • Not a calibrated probability. The three grids come from the same starting data, so they are not independent opinions. Agreement between them is a good sign, not a guarantee. This run has not yet been checked against campus reports and IMD for the coming days.
  • Track record so far (2–3 events): the 3 km grid caught when rain started and stopped on 21 Oct and on the night of 22–23 Oct, but it also gave rain on drizzle-only days and over-estimated the amount on 22 Oct. The 9 km grid was erratic in amount (too low on 21 Oct, several times too high on 17 Oct). The 1 km grid was closest on the drizzle day but placed some rain about 10 km away. This is why amounts are not shown.
  • Last forecast check. The run of 31 Oct 12 UTC gave an 83 % chance of rain (36 % of a heavier amount) for 11:30–14:30 IST and 94 % (52 % heavier) for 14:30–17:30 IST on 2 Nov. Rain did fall on campus that afternoon, and IMD gives 21.8 mm for the IMD day that ends at 08:30 IST on 3 Nov (it includes that afternoon and the following night). In the same run the model gave about 27 mm at the campus point up to 17:30 IST on 2 Nov, so for this event timing and size were both close, but this is one event. The runs of 27 and 29 Oct gave 0 % for the days that stayed dry. Rain amounts are still not shown because the model has been far off in other cases.
  • Timing check, 4 Nov. The run of 3 Nov 00 UTC gave a 62 % chance of rain (32 % heavier) for 14:30–17:30 IST on 4 Nov. Rain reached the campus at about 18:00 IST, roughly three hours after that block, and returned from 21:30 IST. So the model caught the day but put the main rain too early. IMD gridded rainfall for that evening is not yet confirmed, so no amount is compared.
  • Check, 10–11 Nov. The run of 9 Nov 06 UTC gave a 0 % chance of rain near the campus for the whole of 10 and 11 Nov on all three grids. IMD gridded rainfall for the campus cell was 4.2 mm for the IMD day ending 08:30 IST on 10 Nov (3x3-cell mean 2.3 mm) and 0.0 mm for 11 Nov. So the light rain of 10 Nov was missed, and the dry 11 Nov was right. The run of 10 Nov 06 UTC shown here gave 0 % for 11 Nov too, which also matched IMD (0.0 mm). Its 12 Nov forecast is not yet checked because IMD has not published that day. Two checks are too few to judge the model.
  • The forecast is one model run from one set of starting data, and it gets less reliable the further ahead you look.
  • Coastline is simplified. The map opens on the campus region (11–16.4°N, 76.8–82.2°E); “Wide view” shows 7–19°N, 73–85°E (Arabian Sea, Laccadive Sea and Bay of Bengal). The 9 km grid covers everywhere; the finer 3 km grid is used inside the dotted box. The map is smoothed between grid cells and shows rain or no rain, not amounts.
